newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures drift lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures drift lower in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished slightly easier on Friday in thin trade with the absence of fresh buyers weighing heavily on the market, dealers said.

"The market just dried up. We were hoping that some shortcovering would emerge ahead of the holiday in Japan on Monday, but the buying did not come up and the market just drifted lower," a local rubber trader said.
Another dealer said: "There was no pickup this afternoon. It just sort of died because of the absence of fresh buying interest. Volume was very light."
Dealers said the market may drift lower next week in the absence of fresh factors.
"There's no speculative interest which would help in buoying sentiment in the market," one trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 128.50-129.00 U.S. cents a kg from 129.00 cents.

November RSS1 was seen at 184.50-185.50 Singapore cents (US$1.31-$1.32) a kg from Thursday's settlement of 185.50 cents. November TSR20 was quoted at 179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27) a kg against 179.50 cents.
